Deuteronomy 28:12 — *Yahuah (LORD) shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.* *And in those days I will open the store chambers of blessing which are in the heaven, so as to send them down upon the earth over the work and labour of the children of men.* (1 Enoch 11:1)
Moses told the people what Yahuah (God) would do for those who walk in his commandments: open his good treasure of heaven in its season and bless the work of their hands. Enoch sees the same storehouses opened over the work and labour of men, and the promise in both places rests on a people walking in the commandments Yahuah (God) gave.

Malachi 3:10 — *Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.* *And in those days I will open the store chambers of blessing which are in the heaven, so as to send them down upon the earth over the work and labour of the children of men.* (1 Enoch 11:1)
Malachi hears Yahuah (God) say he will open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing past what can be received. Enoch's storehouses of blessing and the prophet's windows of heaven are the same open heaven, given to the earth by the Creator's hand and not taken by men's.
cards.member_note: Malachi 3:10 — *Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.* Malachi hears of the same windows of heaven opened.

Psalm 85:10 — *Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.* *And truth and peace shall be associated together throughout all the days of the world and throughout all the generations of men.’* (1 Enoch 11:2)
The psalmist sees mercy and truth meeting and righteousness and peace kissing, and Enoch says truth and peace will be joined through all the days of the world and all the generations of men. Peace in both places comes with truth beside it, never without it.
cards.member_note: Psalm 85:10 — *Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.* The psalmist sees truth and peace joined as Enoch does.

thread.title: The storehouses of blessing opened, and truth and peace joined for every generation
thread.summary_md:
It ain't new. The close of Enoch's word about the cleansed earth gives the blessing in the very words the Torah and the prophets already used. *And in those days I will open the store chambers of blessing which are in the heaven, so as to send them down upon the earth over the work and labour of the children of men.* (1 Enoch 11:1) Moses told the people who hear Yahuah (God) what he would do: *Yahuah (LORD) shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.* (Deuteronomy 28:12) Malachi hears the same voice and the same open heaven: *Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.* (Malachi 3:10) In neither place is the rain a thing men earn by cleverness or take by force. It is Yahuah's (God's) to give, and he gives it to a people walking in his commandments, which is why the curse that follows in Deuteronomy 28 is the exile judgment for turning away and not the Torah itself.

Then Enoch turns from the rain to the peace that comes with it. *And truth and peace shall be associated together throughout all the days of the world and throughout all the generations of men.’* (1 Enoch 11:2) The psalmist had already seen truth and peace side by side: *Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.* (Psalm 85:10) Truth is not set against peace, and peace is not bought by giving up truth. They are joined, and Enoch says they stay joined through every generation.

So the two verses of this chapter are the open treasure of heaven and the settled peace of the earth, and both were in the Torah and the Psalms before Enoch's book was ever copied. The reader holds them together and hears one voice, the same Yahuah (God) who opened the heaven for Moses and Malachi opening it again for an earth made clean.

cards.note:
Isaiah 41:19 — *I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the shittah tree, and the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the fir tree, and the pine, and the box tree together:* *And thence I went towards the east, into the midst of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness and it was solitary, full of trees and plants.* (1 Enoch 28:1)
Enoch walks into a solitary wilderness and finds it full of trees and plants. Isaiah hears Yahuah (God) say he will plant that very kind of wilderness with trees, so the desert is something he fills and not something he abandons.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 41:19 — *I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the shittah tree, and the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the fir tree, and the pine, and the box tree together:* Isaiah promises trees planted in the wilderness.

cards.note:
Isaiah 35:6 — *Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.* *And water gushed forth from above.* (1 Enoch 28:2)
Water gushing out in the desert is what Isaiah promised when he said waters would break out in the wilderness and streams in the desert. The place that looked dry and empty holds a spring that Yahuah (God) opens.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 35:6 — *Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.* Isaiah promises the same waters in the desert.

cards.note:
Genesis 2:6 — *But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.* *Rushing like a copious watercourse [which flowed] towards the north- west it caused clouds and dew to ascend on every side.* (1 Enoch 28:3)
The watercourse in Enoch's vision sends clouds and dew up on every side, and in the garden narrative a mist went up from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground. It is the same watering of the ground, rising from the earth by the Creator's order.
cards.member_note: Genesis 2:6 — *But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.* The first watering of the ground rose from the earth as Enoch sees.

thread.title: The wilderness with trees and living water — what Yahuah does with a desert
thread.summary_md:
It ain't new. On his journey Enoch comes to a wilderness that looks empty and finds it alive. *And thence I went towards the east, into the midst of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness and it was solitary, full of trees and plants.* (1 Enoch 28:1) Isaiah had said Yahuah (God) would do exactly this to a desert: *I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the shittah tree, and the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the fir tree, and the pine, and the box tree together:* (Isaiah 41:19) The water Enoch sees pouring out is the water Isaiah promised: *And water gushed forth from above.* (1 Enoch 28:2) *Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.* (Isaiah 35:6) In both places the wilderness is not a punishment that stays. It is the place where Yahuah (God) opens a spring and plants trees, and the same wilderness is where the prophets bring the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) on the way home.

The last verse reaches back past the prophets to the first pages of Genesis. *Rushing like a copious watercourse [which flowed] towards the north- west it caused clouds and dew to ascend on every side.* (1 Enoch 28:3) Before rain fell, the ground was watered another way: *But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.* (Genesis 2:6) Enoch's clouds and dew rising on every side are the Creator's own way of watering the ground, seen again in a dry place, so the wilderness and the garden were never two separate works.

A short passage of travel in Enoch's book therefore stands on a Genesis foundation and a prophetic promise. The hand that made the first garden is the hand that sends water up in the desert and plants it, and the reader sees that the desert is where he works as he did in the beginning.

cards.note:
Jude 1:6 — *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* *Therefore all that is hidden shall come upon them for ever and ever; for neither angel nor man shall have his portion (in it), but alone they have received their judgement for ever and ever.’* (1 Enoch 68:5)
Michael says the judgement on the fallen angels is for ever and ever, and that they alone have received it. Jude says the angels who left their own habitation are reserved in everlasting chains for the judgment of the great day, which is the same verdict in the same terms.
cards.member_note: Jude 1:6 — *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* Jude gives the same everlasting judgement on the angels who left their place.

cards.note:
Isaiah 14:14 — *I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the El Elyon (most High).* *And it came to pass when he stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, Michael said thus to Raphael: ‘I will not take their part under the eye of Yahuah (Lord); for Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits has been angry with them because they do as if they were Yahuah (Lord).* (1 Enoch 68:4)
Michael will not plead for the angels because they did as if they were Yahuah (the Lord). Isaiah gives the words of that pride in the mouth of the one brought down, I will be like the El Elyon (Most High), so the reader hears what taking the place of Yahuah (God) sounds like.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 14:14 — *I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the El Elyon (most High).* The pride that Michael refuses to excuse is named in the prophet's own words.

cards.note:
Jude 1:9 — *Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, Yahuah (Lord) rebuke thee.* *And on that day Michael answered Raphael and said: ‘The power of the spirit transports and makes me to tremble because of the severity of the judgement of the secrets, the judgement of the angels: who can endure the severe judgement which has been executed, and before which they melt away?’* (1 Enoch 68:2)
Even Michael trembles at the severity of the judgement on the angels and will not take their part. Jude also shows Michael unwilling to bring a railing accusation and leaving the rebuke with Yahuah (the Lord), which fits an archangel who judges nothing for himself.
cards.member_note: Jude 1:9 — *Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, Yahuah (Lord) rebuke thee.* Jude shows Michael leaving the rebuke with Yahuah.

thread.title: Michael will not take their part — the judgement that Jude also names
thread.summary_md:
It ain't new. Noah hears two great angels speak, and what he hears is how heavy the judgement on the fallen angels is. *And it came to pass when he stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, Michael said thus to Raphael: ‘I will not take their part under the eye of Yahuah (Lord); for Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits has been angry with them because they do as if they were Yahuah (Lord).* (1 Enoch 68:4) Michael will not plead for them, because they did as if they were Yahuah (the Lord) himself, and Isaiah had already given the words of that pride: *I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the El Elyon (most High).* (Isaiah 14:14) Taking the place that belongs to Yahuah (God) is the root of the fall, and Michael will not make an excuse for it.

Jude carries the same verdict into the letters of the apostles. *Therefore all that is hidden shall come upon them for ever and ever; for neither angel nor man shall have his portion (in it), but alone they have received their judgement for ever and ever.’* (1 Enoch 68:5) The angels who received that judgement are the ones Jude describes: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* (Jude 1:6) Jude also shows Michael in the same posture, the archangel who will not bring a railing accusation on his own authority: *Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, Yahuah (Lord) rebuke thee.* (Jude 1:9) He does not take Yahuah's (God's) judging into his own hands, and he does not soften it either.

So a chapter that some readers wave off as strange stands on the same ground as Jude and Isaiah. The angels who left their place are chained until the day, Michael and Raphael do not speak for them, and the pride behind it all is the wish to be like the El Elyon (Most High). The reader sees that Jude was not quoting a stray legend but standing on a record the assembly already had.

cards.note:
Isaiah 14:12 — *How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!* *And again I saw with mine eyes as I slept, and I saw the heaven above, and behold a star fell from heaven, and it arose and eat and pastured amongst those oxen.* (1 Enoch 86:1)
In Enoch's vision a star falls from heaven and begins to graze among the oxen, and Isaiah asks how one was fallen from heaven and cut down to the ground. A star that falls is what the prophet's words picture too, a bright one brought down and found on the earth.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 14:12 — *How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!* The prophet asks the same question of a bright one fallen to the earth.

cards.note:
Genesis 6:2 — *That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* *And again I saw in the vision, and looked towards the heaven, and behold I saw many stars descend and cast themselves down from heaven to that first star, and they became bulls amongst those cattle and pastured with them [amongst them].* (1 Enoch 86:3)
Many stars come down after the first and become bulls among the cattle, and Genesis says the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men and took wives of all which they chose. Enoch shows the descent that Genesis tells in a single line, with the heavenly ones taking what they were not given.
cards.member_note: Genesis 6:2 — *That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* Genesis tells in one line what the dream shows in the descent of the stars.

cards.note:
Genesis 6:4 — *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* *And I looked at them and saw, and behold they all let out their privy members, like horses, and began to cover the cows of the oxen, and they all became pregnant and bare elephants, camels, and asses.* (1 Enoch 86:4)
The cows become pregnant and bear elephants, camels and asses, and Genesis says the sons of Elohim (God) came in to the daughters of men and their children became the giants. Enoch pictures the unnatural offspring as beasts of the field and does not dress it up.
cards.member_note: Genesis 6:4 — *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* Genesis names the children that the dream pictures as beasts.

cards.note:
Genesis 6:11 — *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence.* *And they began, moreover, to devour those oxen; and behold all the children of the earth began to tremble and quake before them and to flee from them.* (1 Enoch 86:6)
The children of the earth tremble and flee as the new creatures devour, and Genesis says the earth was corrupt before Elohim (God) and was filled with violence. The terror in the vision is the violence that brought the flood.
cards.member_note: Genesis 6:11 — *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence.* The terror in the dream is the violence that Genesis says filled the earth.

thread.title: The stars fall to the cattle, and the earth is filled with violence
thread.summary_md:
Enoch's second dream gives the story of the Watchers as an animal parable, and the picture is plain once Genesis is beside it. *And again I saw in the vision, and looked towards the heaven, and behold I saw many stars descend and cast themselves down from heaven to that first star, and they became bulls amongst those cattle and pastured with them [amongst them].* (1 Enoch 86:3) Genesis tells the descent in one sentence: *That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* (Genesis 6:2) The dream shows what the sentence meant. The ones who came down joined the cattle of the earth, and the seed line of Adam, which the oxen stand for, was crossed by something that was not of it.

The next verses give the result. *And I looked at them and saw, and behold they all let out their privy members, like horses, and began to cover the cows of the oxen, and they all became pregnant and bare elephants, camels, and asses.* (1 Enoch 86:4) Genesis names the same children: *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* (Genesis 6:4) The elephants, camels and asses are the dream's picture of offspring that were not the kind the Creator had made, and the seed of promise, which runs through the fathers, was the very thing under attack.

Then the cost comes down on the earth. *And they began, moreover, to devour those oxen; and behold all the children of the earth began to tremble and quake before them and to flee from them.* (1 Enoch 86:6) Genesis tells the end of it in the verse that opens the flood: *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence.* (Genesis 6:11) The trembling children of the earth in the dream and the earth filled with violence in Genesis are one scene seen from two sides. The library holds Enoch's dream beside Genesis so the reader can see in full what Genesis compressed.

cards.note:
Isaiah 26:21 — *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.* *And when sin and unrighteousness and blasphemy And violence in all kinds of deeds increase, And apostasy and transgression and uncleanness increase, A great chastisement shall come from heaven upon all these, And the holy Yahuah (Lord) will come forth with wrath and chastisement To execute judgement on earth.* (1 Enoch 91:7)
Enoch says the holy Yahuah (Lord) will come forth with wrath to execute judgement on the earth, and Isaiah says Yahuah (the LORD) comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. Both see the day as Yahuah's own coming, with the earth giving up what it had covered.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 26:21 — *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.* Isaiah sees the same coming of Yahuah to judge the earth.

cards.note:
Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* *And the righteous shall arise from their sleep, And wisdom shall arise and be given unto them.* (1 Enoch 91:10)
Enoch says the righteous will arise from their sleep and wisdom will be given to them, and Daniel says many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake. The sleepers are the same sleepers, and the waking is promised in both places.
cards.member_note: Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* Daniel sees the same sleepers wake.

cards.note:
Haggai 2:9 — *The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): and in this place will I give peace, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* *And at its close they shall acquire houses through their righteousness, And a house shall be built for the Great King in glory for evermore,* (1 Enoch 91:13)
Enoch says a house shall be built for the Great King in glory for evermore, and Haggai hears that the glory of the latter house will be greater than the former, with peace given in that place. The house that is promised is greater than the one men had built before.
cards.member_note: Haggai 2:9 — *The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): and in this place will I give peace, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* Haggai hears of the same latter house, greater than the former.

cards.note:
Isaiah 65:17 — *For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.* *And the first heaven shall depart and pass away, And a new heaven shall appear, And all the powers of the heavens shall give sevenfold light.* (1 Enoch 91:16)
Enoch says the first heaven will pass away and a new heaven will appear, and Isaiah hears Yahuah (God) say he creates new heavens and a new earth. The new heaven is a promise the prophets made before Enoch's book, and it ends the long count of weeks.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 65:17 — *For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.* Isaiah hears of the same new heavens and new earth.

thread.title: The weeks of Enoch — the judgement, the house for the Great King, and the new heaven
thread.summary_md:
It ain't new. Enoch calls his sons together and gives them the shape of the ages, and the shape is the one the prophets already drew. *And when sin and unrighteousness and blasphemy And violence in all kinds of deeds increase, And apostasy and transgression and uncleanness increase, A great chastisement shall come from heaven upon all these, And the holy Yahuah (Lord) will come forth with wrath and chastisement To execute judgement on earth.* (1 Enoch 91:7) Isaiah says the same of the day: *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.* (Isaiah 26:21) The judgement is Yahuah (God) himself coming out of his place.

The sleeping righteous come next. *And the righteous shall arise from their sleep, And wisdom shall arise and be given unto them.* (1 Enoch 91:10) Daniel saw the same waking: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2)

Then the eighth week brings a house for the Great King, and Haggai had heard of a house greater than any men built before it: *The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): and in this place will I give peace, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* (Haggai 2:9) The count ends with the heaven itself made new. *And the first heaven shall depart and pass away, And a new heaven shall appear, And all the powers of the heavens shall give sevenfold light.* (1 Enoch 91:16) Isaiah heard the same word from Yahuah (God): *For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.* (Isaiah 65:17)

The weeks are Enoch's way of walking his sons through the ages, from violence to judgement, to the sleepers rising, to the house, to the new heaven, and each stop has a verse in the Tanakh that says the same.

cards.note:
Isaiah 40:26 — *Lift up your eyes on high, and behold who hath created these things, that bringeth out their host by number: he calleth them all by names by the greatness of his might, for that he is strong in power; not one faileth.* *Observe the heaven, ye children of heaven, and every work of the El Elyon (Most High), and fear ye Him and work no evil in His presence.* (1 Enoch 101:1)
Enoch tells the children of heaven to observe the heaven and every work of the El Elyon (Most High), and Isaiah tells the people to lift up their eyes on high and see who created these things. Looking at the heavens is how both of them lead the reader to fear their Maker.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 40:26 — *Lift up your eyes on high, and behold who hath created these things, that bringeth out their host by number: he calleth them all by names by the greatness of his might, for that he is strong in power; not one faileth.* Isaiah sends the people to look at the heavens and see who made them.

cards.note:
Deuteronomy 11:17 — *And then the LORD’S wrath be kindled against you, and he shut up the heaven, that there be no rain, and that the land yield not her fruit; and lest ye perish quickly from off the good land which Yahuah (LORD) giveth you.* *If He closes the windows of heaven, and withholds the rain and the dew from descending on the earth on your account, what will ye do then?* (1 Enoch 101:2)
Enoch asks what sinners will do if the El Elyon (Most High) closes the windows of heaven and withholds the rain and dew, and Moses had already told the people that a shut heaven with no rain is the answer to turning from the commandments. The warning is Torah before it is Enoch.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 11:17 — *And then the LORD’S wrath be kindled against you, and he shut up the heaven, that there be no rain, and that the land yield not her fruit; and lest ye perish quickly from off the good land which Yahuah (LORD) giveth you.* Moses had already named the shut heaven as the answer to turning from the commandments.

cards.note:
Jeremiah 5:22 — *Fear ye not me? saith Yahuah (LORD): will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?* *Are not the entire sea and all its waters, and all its movements, the work of the El Elyon (Most High), and has He not set limits to its doings, and confined it throughout by the sand?* (1 Enoch 101:6)
Enoch says the El Elyon (Most High) has set limits to the sea and confined it by the sand, and Jeremiah hears Yahuah (God) ask whether his people do not fear him who placed the sand for the bound of the sea. The sand that holds the sea is the same sign in both books, set up to be seen and feared.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 5:22 — *Fear ye not me? saith Yahuah (LORD): will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?* Jeremiah points to the sand that bounds the sea as the sign to fear Yahuah.

cards.note:
Psalm 107:26 — *They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble.* *And see ye not the sailors of the ships, how their ships are tossed to and fro by the waves, and are shaken by the winds, and are in sore trouble?* (1 Enoch 101:4)
Enoch asks the sinners whether they do not see the sailors tossed to and fro by the waves in sore trouble, and the psalmist writes of those who go down to the sea in ships and mount up to heaven and go down to the depths with their soul melted. The sailors know their fear and sinners should know theirs.
cards.member_note: Psalm 107:26 — *They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble.* The psalmist pictures the same trouble of men in ships on the sea.

thread.title: Observe the sea and the sky — the works that teach the fear of the Most High
thread.summary_md:
It ain't new. The chapter calls the reader to look at the works of Yahuah (God), and the call matches the Tanakh. *If He closes the windows of heaven, and withholds the rain and the dew from descending on the earth on your account, what will ye do then?* (1 Enoch 101:2) Moses told Yashar'el (Israel) in the land what a shut heaven meant: *And then the LORD’S wrath be kindled against you, and he shut up the heaven, that there be no rain, and that the land yield not her fruit; and lest ye perish quickly from off the good land which Yahuah (LORD) giveth you.* (Deuteronomy 11:17) The rain and the dew are given to a people walking in his commandments and withheld when they turn from them.

The sea is the second teacher. *Are not the entire sea and all its waters, and all its movements, the work of the El Elyon (Most High), and has He not set limits to its doings, and confined it throughout by the sand?* (1 Enoch 101:6) Jeremiah hears Yahuah (God) use the same sign against a people that did not fear him: *Fear ye not me? saith Yahuah (LORD): will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?* (Jeremiah 5:22) The sand that holds the sea is a small thing that stops a great thing, a sign anyone can see. Enoch's sailors know the sea can swallow them, while sinners on the land have the same Maker above them and feel no fear.

So Enoch's exhortation is the voice of the whole Tanakh. Look at the heaven, look at the sea, and fear the Maker who set both in their order. Each line of the chapter sits beside a verse from Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah or the Psalms, and the reader sees the book repeating what the prophets already said.

Enoch says the righteous are the guides of the children of earth and a recompense over the whole earth, and Daniel says the wise will shine as the brightness of the firmament and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever. Enoch says Yahuah (the Lord) bade them summon and testify to the children of earth, and Yahuah (God) tells Ezekiel he is made a watchman to give warning from his mouth. The testimony is given because it was first given to the one who testifies.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 3:17 — *Son of Adam, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Yashar'el (Israel): therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.* Ezekiel is made a watchman to give warning from the mouth of Yahuah.

Amen.* (1 Enoch 105:2)
Enoch ends with peace for the children of uprightness, and Isaiah says the work of righteousness shall be peace and its effect quietness and assurance for ever. Peace follows righteousness in both places and does not come ahead of it.

Enoch says the giants will be born not according to the spirit but according to the flesh, and Genesis says there were giants in the earth in those days. The child of Lamech is not one of them, but Lamech's own son in the line of Adam.

Enoch says Noah and his sons will be saved from the destruction that will come on the earth, and Genesis says everything living was destroyed and Noah only remained alive with those who were with him in the ark. The child Lamech feared is the one Yahuah (God) kept for the flood.
cards.member_note: Genesis 7:23 — *And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.* Genesis records that Noah only remained alive with those in the ark.

Enoch says the child born to Lamech will be left on the earth with his three children saved with him, and Peter says few, that is eight souls, were saved by water while the ark was being prepared. The three sons and their wives are the ones Enoch sees ahead of time.

thread.title: The birth of Noah — the child of Lamech and the seed kept through the flood
thread.summary_md:
It ain't new. Lamech sees a newborn son who shines like the sun and fears the child is not his own. Methuselah goes to Enoch for the truth, and Enoch answers by naming what was happening in the days of Jared: *And behold they commit sin and transgress the law, and have united themselves with women and commit sin with them, and have married some of them, and have begot children by them.* (1 Enoch 106:14) That is the Genesis account in a sentence: *That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* (Genesis 6:2) Enoch tells Methuselah the child is in truth Lamech's son, and the line of the fathers is unbroken.

He goes on to the giants and the flood. *And they shall produce on the earth giants not according to the spirit, but according to the flesh, and there shall be a great punishment on the earth, and the earth shall be cleansed from all impurity.* (1 Enoch 106:17) Genesis states the same fact: *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* (Genesis 6:4) The giants come of the flesh and not the spirit, and the flood is the answer. Yet one house is kept, as Genesis tells it: *And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.* (Genesis 7:23) Peter, writing long after, counts the saved: *Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of Elohim (God) waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.* (1 Peter 3:20)

So Enoch's account of the birth stands with the Torah and the letter of Peter, all telling one story: the Watchers fell, the earth was filled with violence, and the seed of the fathers was kept through the water in one house. The reader sees why the paternal line was worth guarding.

Psalm 24:6 — *This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.* *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1)
Enoch reads in the heavenly tablets that a generation of righteousness will arise, and the psalmist names that kind of people as the generation of those who seek him and seek his face. The righteous generation is made up of those who seek Yahuah (God).
cards.member_note: Psalm 24:6 — *This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.* The psalmist names the generation that seeks Yahuah.

cards.note:
Daniel 9:24 — *Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.* *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1)
Enoch sees transgression destroyed and sin passing away from the earth, and Daniel hears that the time is determined to finish the transgression and make an end of sins and bring in everlasting righteousness. Both look to a day when sin comes to its end.
cards.member_note: Daniel 9:24 — *Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.* Daniel hears of the end of transgression and sin.

cards.note:
Genesis 5:29 — *And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which Yahuah (LORD) hath cursed.* *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3)
Methuselah names the child Noah because he will comfort the earth after all the destruction, and Lamech named him in Genesis for the comfort he would bring concerning the toil of the ground Yahuah (God) had cursed. The name Noah carries the promise in both accounts.
cards.member_note: Genesis 5:29 — *And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which Yahuah (LORD) hath cursed.* Lamech names his son for comfort over the cursed ground.

cards.note:
Genesis 8:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) smelled a sweet savour; and Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.* *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3)
Methuselah is told that Noah will comfort the earth after all the destruction, and Genesis shows it coming true when Yahuah (God) smelled the sweet savour after the flood and said he would not again curse the ground for man's sake.
cards.member_note: Genesis 8:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) smelled a sweet savour; and Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.* The comfort in the name came true when Yahuah would not again curse the ground.

cards.note: Genesis 5:28 — *And Lamech lived an hundred eighty and two years, and begat a son:* *And now, my son, go and make known to thy son Lamech that this son, which has been born, is in truth his son, and that (this) is no lie.’* (1 Enoch 107:2) Genesis records the birth in one plain line, Lamech begat a son, and Enoch's answer to Lamech's fear is just as plain: the boy is his, and that is no lie. The strange brightness of the child did not put him outside the line of Adam; he stands in it, and the flood will be the proof.
cards.member_note: Genesis 5:28 — *And Lamech lived an hundred eighty and two years, and begat a son:* The plain record of the birth that Enoch confirms is true.

cards.note: Genesis 6:11 — *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence.* *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1) What Enoch read on the tablets as generation upon generation transgressing is what Genesis says of the earth before the flood: corrupt before Elohim (God), and filled with violence. The judgement comes because the transgression was a pattern, not a single crime, and it ends only when a generation of righteousness arises.
cards.member_note: Genesis 6:11 — *the earth was filled with violence.* Genesis gives the same verdict over the same earth.
